summary: nuvyra-marketplace-sdk auto-loads unrelated 'htps-provider' dependency at import time
details: On require of nuvyra-marketplace-sdk, dist/index.js unconditionally invokes initializeProvider(), which dynamically requires the third-party dependency 'htps-provider' and instantiates its HttpProvider on every import. The dependency name resembles 'https-provider' and has no functional relationship to the package's advertised purpose (an Ethereum marketplace SDK). The dynamic import is wrapped in an empty try/catch that swallows errors, and success is masked by a misleading 'Server is running successfully!' console message inside what is presented as a client SDK. Any consumer that imports nuvyra-marketplace-sdk transitively executes code from htps-provider at import time; because the executed code lives in a separately-resolved package unrelated to the SDK's stated function and is loaded behind cover-story logging, this is a trojan-loader pattern that hands import-time code execution to the external dependency.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
